validation_scope: Contextual strategy-family scheduling over a 20-item philosophy/method library.  The bypass compares an ACP-aware scheduler against an immediate-utility baseline on expert-labeled tasks, cross-domain transfer cases, and boundary traps.

strategies.name: controlled_intervention
strategies.claim: When confounders make evidence ambiguous, isolate one variable and compare matched controls.

strategies.name: incremental_replacement
strategies.claim: When a working baseline and module boundary exist, replace one component at a time.

strategies.name: divide_and_conquer
strategies.claim: Split independent subproblems before optimizing the whole system.

strategies.name: abduction
strategies.claim: Generate the best explanatory hypothesis when observations are sparse but patterned.

strategies.name: deduction
strategies.claim: Apply known rules when premises and operators are reliable.

strategies.name: induction
strategies.claim: Infer a general rule from repeated observations when sampling is representative.

strategies.name: analogy
strategies.claim: Transfer a solution when role structure and invariants are preserved.

strategies.name: reductio
strategies.claim: Assume the target claim and derive contradiction to expose impossibility.

strategies.name: proof_by_contradiction
strategies.claim: Prove by negating the target and showing inconsistency.

strategies.name: occam
strategies.claim: Prefer simpler explanations when fit is comparable and data are limited.

strategies.name: bayesian_update
strategies.claim: Update priors with calibrated evidence instead of replacing beliefs from one observation.

strategies.name: minimal_prototype
strategies.claim: Build the smallest runnable version when feasibility is uncertain.

strategies.name: counterexample_guided_refinement
strategies.claim: Use failing cases to refine the rule rather than averaging them away.

strategies.name: boundary_case_analysis
strategies.claim: Probe edge cases when a rule may fail outside its intended scope.

strategies.name: negative_control
strategies.claim: Test a condition that should not improve to detect leakage or over-transfer.

strategies.name: model_comparison
strategies.claim: Compare competing models under the same evidence and objective.

strategies.name: error_decomposition
strategies.claim: Separate error sources before proposing a new solution.

strategies.name: invariant_seeking
strategies.claim: Look for preserved quantities or relations across transformations.

strategies.name: causal_intervention
strategies.claim: Act on a variable to test whether it changes the outcome.

strategies.name: feedback_stabilization
strategies.claim: When growth triggers opposing forces, model convergence and control loops.

tasks.prompt: Replace one recursive runner module while keeping old v2 phases.
Determine if a new prompt or judge caused the win.
A QA pipeline has independent retrieval, rerank, reader, and judge failures.
A repeated anomaly has few samples but a shared pattern.
Known premises imply a deterministic target answer.
Many representative examples suggest a general trend.
An economics feedback case has preserved roles with a physics example.
A tempting analogy lacks negative controls and may leak answer context.
A repair works in center cases but may fail at edge cases.
Failures mix retrieval errors, execution mistakes, and judge defects.
Several candidate policies use the same evidence and objective metric.
Demand growth triggers an opposing supply or price response.

interpretation: Full-v2 Phase 5 makes method/philosophy selection operational: strategy families are assumption nodes with scope and failure boundaries, and the scheduler chooses them from task context, ACP, risk, cost, and boundary evidence instead of relying on prompt-level explanation.
